propositions: T1 (a BLOCKING plan-review criterion) lost its server-side web-search grounding tool on cutover to Bedrock because the tool attachment gate used a provider-name prefix match ("anthropic") rather than capability-registry membership, and bedrock-qualified Claude reports a different name.

The silent withdrawal was undetectable in signed verdicts because provider_provenance.capabilities did not record whether web access was actually attached, making the degradation invisible to readers.

The original design deliberately avoided rebar-side HTTP fetch tooling; fixing this requires either measuring whether Bedrock's Converse API can carry Anthropic's native tool, or building a rebar-side mechanism with explicit egress/caching/injection-risk controls.

The web-search decision must be relocated from anthropic_model.py to capabilities.py and must take no model or provider-name input, deriving the decision from capability-registry membership only, consistent with the epic's zero-exceptions rule against prefix matching.

Every plan-review run on every provider must attach web access for T1, verified by execution not by gate-condition inspection, with the attached capability and its absence both recorded in signed verdicts.
